artworks.title: The Eagle of Saint John
artworks.artist: Martin Schongauer
artworks.medium: engraving
artworks.creditLine: Rosenwald Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a bird within a circular medallion. The bird has a long neck, sharp claws, and outstretched wings with detailed feathering. It stands with one foot slightly raised while holding a flowing banner or ribbon within the medallion's design. The head of the bird is portrayed with a serene expression and there is a halo behind it. The background is simple. The drawing is detailed with clear lines, emphasizing the texture of the feathers and the grace of the composition.

artworks.title: River Landscape with Two Buildings
artworks.artist: Augustin Hirschvogel
artworks.medium: etching
artworks.creditLine: Rosenwald Collection
artworks.description: The image shows a townscape with architectural elements set against a mountainous backdrop. The view is slightly elevated, revealing details of the buildings near a body of water. The horizon is high, with distant hills and mountains in the background. A large tower-like structure is on the right, displaying fine line work. In the center, a group of buildings leads to a bridge with arches. A tall tree is on the left with delicate branches and foliage. The color palette is monochromatic, emphasizing the detailed line work and shading.

artworks.title: Great American Cock
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: A wild turkey standing among tall grasses and reeds against a cream-white background nearly fills this vertical, hand-colored etching. The bird’s body faces our right, and its pale, steel-blue, scrawny neck, small head, and short beak turn to look to our left in profile. Pink bulges line the bird’s neck, and its dark eye is wide and alert. A triangular, short, horn-like protrusion over the beak appears to be covered in fuzz. The turkey’s stout and robust body is covered with golden-orange feathers down its back and around the breast. Black and white striped wings are tucked along its body below, and the tawny-brown feathers of its tail fans out to nearly brush the ground. Feathers where the bird’s ribbed and scaly, pale pink and gray legs meet the body are striped ruby red and black. The bird strides to our right on a dirt ground with tufts of plants. The reeds, some of them bamboo-like, fade in the background around the turkey. Text at the top center of the print reads, “PLATE 1.” The artist’s name is printed below the image under the left corner: “Drawn by J.J. Audubon M.W.S.” Printed cursive text across the bottom margin of the page reads, “Great American Cock Male” and block letters read, “VULGO (WILD TURKEY--) Meleagris Gallopavo. A printed inscription under the right corner reads, “Engraved by W. H. Lizars. Edinr.”

artworks.title: Yellow-billed Cuckoo
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two birds are depicted amongst green leaves, with one bird holding a large butterfly in its beak, and another bird perched on a branch below. The color palette includes primarily green, brown, black, and white, with a touch of yellow on the butterfly. The leaves cover most of the upper portion of the image, while the birds occupy the central area with their wings spread. A cluster of reddish-brown fruits hangs below the birds in the lower left corner.

artworks.title: Prothonotary Warbler
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two brightly colored birds perched on a vine among green leaves. The colors include vibrant yellows and oranges for the birds, complemented by the green leaves and a beige background. The birds are in different positions on the vine.

artworks.title: Purple Finch
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds perched on tree branches. The painting depicts three finches, each perched on branches adorned with pine needles and pinkish cones. Two of the birds exhibit vibrant reds in their plumage, while the third features more muted browns and greys. The branches they sit upon are artistically detailed, capturing the texture of the bark and the structure of the cones and needles meticulously. The composition is calm and elegant, highlighting the beauty and diversity of these birds.

artworks.title: Bonaparte Fly Catcher
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a small bird perched on a branch with large green leaves and a cluster of pink flowers. The bird has a blue-grey head, yellow chest, and olive-grey wings. The branch shows some spots of natural wear and extends to a cluster of pinkish-red tubular flowers.

artworks.title: Great American Hen and Young
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a wild turkey hen with her young. The scene depicts a large, richly colored female turkey with a flock of her poults. The female turkey has a striking plumage with shades of brown, rust, and a hint of iridescent greens. Her extended tail feathers and poised posture suggest attentiveness. The young turkeys are scattered around her, moving through a lush meadow filled with grasses and green foliage. The background is adorned with plants and wildflowers.

artworks.title: Purple Grackle
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting features two blackbirds among corn plants. The birds are shown among the green leaves of the corn plants. One bird is perched on the corn, while the other is slightly above with outspread wings. The corn plants are depicted in different stages of growth, with tassels and ears visible. The painting highlights the black and iridescent feathers of the birds against the green backdrop of the corn. This artwork is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: White-throated Sparrow
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a flowering branch, depicting two white-throated sparrows balancing on a branch of a tree. The sparrows have brown and gray plumage with a yellow patch above their beaks. The artwork showcases the details of the birds and the flowers around them, following the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Selby's Flycatcher
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a yellow and olive-green bird on a slender green stem with delicate green foliage and two red flowers at the top. The color palette includes shades of green, yellow, and red. The bird is positioned on the stem, while the flowers are at the top. The background is a muted cream color.

artworks.title: Brown Lark
artworks.artist: William Home Lizars after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on Whatman paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two birds, identified as a male and female Brown Lark, are perched on a mound of earth adorned with small mushrooms and grass, and a small insect flies above them in the center of the image. The color palette consists of earthy browns for the birds and mound, with touches of green in the grass and subtle hints of grey and white in the birds' feathers and the mushrooms. The male bird is on the left side of the image standing on the mound, and the female bird is positioned to the right, slightly higher on the mound, with both looking upwards towards the insect hovering above.

artworks.title: The Bird of Washington or Great American Sea Eagle
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a large bird of prey standing on a rock. The bird is depicted with attention to detail, showcasing its impressive talons gripping a rocky surface. Its feathers are rendered in shades of brown and black, with the wings folded along its body. The head is turned to the side, highlighting the bird's beak and eye. The overall composition focuses on the bird's majesty and power, with shading adding depth to the plumage. The image reflects a naturalistic and realistic style.

artworks.title: Baltimore Oriole
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Three orange, black, and white birds nestle among wide leaves and round, pale pink and yellow flowers in this hand-colored engraving. Two of the birds have vivid orange markings edged with black and white. One near the top right corner is numbered with a tiny 1 and the one below with a 2. Numbered 3, a female is muted in tone, and she perches on a sack-shaped nest hanging from the plant’s stem. All three birds face and are angled toward the center of the composition, which is mostly veiled with wide green leaves around three blossoms. Engraved text in the lower center of the print reads, “Baltimore Oriole, 1. & 2. Males, 3. Female and Nest, Icterus Baltimore. Plant Vulgo. Yellow Poplar. Lirodendron Tulipifera.” An inscription in the bottom left corner reads, “Drawn from Nature by John J. Audobon, F.R.S.E. M.W.S.” and another in the lower right corner reads, “Engraved by R. Havell Junior.” Fainter text below is difficult to make out.

artworks.title: Snow-Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a tree branch with dark berries. The artwork features two birds, one poised attentively, with its tail raised and wings slightly spread, while the other maintains a more calm posture. They both exhibit a mix of dark slate-blue and white coloring, set against a backdrop of a simple tree branch adorned with dangling dark berries. The minimal background enhances the delicate detailing of the birds’ feathers and the texture of the twigs and berries.

artworks.title: Prairie Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two birds perched on tall grass stalks with flowers. The birds are yellow with black and olive-green accents. One bird faces upward and the other faces sideways. The plants extend vertically through the center, with leaves and fronds diverging across the image.

artworks.title: Blue Yellow-backed Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two small birds perched on a tall, slender stem of a flowering plant with pink and yellow flowers at the top. The birds have blue, yellow, white, and black plumage. The plant has narrow green leaves rising along the central stem. One bird is higher up than the other, with both birds positioned on different leaves. The background is plain and light-colored.

artworks.title: Great Footed Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two large falcons with wings spread wide, positioned over a recently killed duck lying on a rocky surface. The color palette is naturalistic, with deep browns and blacks in the falcons' plumage, contrasted by patches of white, and touches of vibrant yellow on their talons and around their eyes. The duck displays dull reds, greens, and blues. Positioned prominently in the center, the falcon on the left has its wings outstretched, while the falcon on the right is bending down towards the duck, with a small, detached feather seen in the air between them.

artworks.title: Carolina Pigeon or Turtle Dove
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of two pairs of doves perched among blooming flowers and leafy branches. At the top of the print, two doves are perched on a branch, looking off to the left. Below them, nestled amidst lush green leaves and large, white flowers, lies a nest containing another dove near the bottom-right corner. The fourth dove perches next to the nest, appearing to feed the bird in the nest something from its beak. The birds have brown and blue plumage on their backs, wings, and heads, while their chests and faces are a pale-yellow color. Their tails end in vibrant blue and white feathers. The background behind the branches and leaves is blank, off-white paper. There are some lines of text under the print.

artworks.title: Bewick's Long-tailed Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Bewick's Long-Tailed Wren perched on a branch. The bird is illustrated with detailed brown and grey feathers and uplifted tail on an Iron Wood branch with green leaves. The composition is elegant with a plain background, emphasizing the bird and branch. The painting features intricate textures of feathers and leaves in a traditional, naturalist style.

artworks.title: Louisiana Water Thrush
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird perched on a leafy stem with a cluster of red berries at the top. The image depicts a detailed and realistic illustration of a bird known as the "Louisiana Water Thrush" showing its intricate plumage in shades of brown, beige, and white. The bird is portrayed mid-song, with its beak open, perched on a slender, curved branch. Below the bird are large, drooping leaves in a deep, almost velvety green, with edges showing signs of browning and curling. At the top of the composition is a conspicuous cluster of bright red berries that contrast against the earthy color palette. The background is a pale, neutral color, emphasizing the natural details and colors of the bird and plant life represented. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Blue-winged Yellow Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James

artworks.title: The Mocking Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This print features four birds and a rattlesnake surrounding a nest that is nestled among yellow flowering vines. The snake is in the center of the print, its mouth open and teeth visible as it lunges to the left towards one of the birds. Another bird is behind it, appearing to peck its yellow eye. Two more birds perch on branches above the nest, looking down. Two of the four birds have blue bodies, and two have black-and-white bodies; they all have black-and-white wings and tails. The nest in the center of the tangle of sticks and flowering vines contains a few small, blue-green eggs. The background behind the nest and birds is beige paper.

artworks.title: Purple Martin
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Three birds are shown around a large, gourd-shaped nest. Two birds are perched on branches, while one is inside the nest. The birds have varying plumage colors - blue and black, gray, black, and white. The color palette includes blues, blacks, browns, grays, and neutrals with a light background. The nest is central, with one bird inside and the others interacting with it.
